Commit the study's code before a render

Source: R/study_render_commit.R
study_render_commit.Rd

Commits the same allow-listed snapshot study_checkpoint takes (code, identity and reproducibility files; never data or outputs) to this copy's render ref in the private repository .checkpoint/repo/, and returns the commit. A render calls it before the job runs, so each figure can print the commit of the code that drew it.

Usage

study_render_commit(job, root = study_root())

Arguments

job

Character(1). The job being rendered, relative to the study root.

root

Character(1). The study root. Default study_root().

Value

Invisibly, the 40-character commit ID.

Details

The job must be in the commit, as the bytes on disk: a job the allow-list leaves out (a symbolic link, a file under a data or estimates folder or one over 50 MB) stops the call rather than returning a commit from which the job cannot be recovered.

A study whose snapshot is unchanged since the last render commit gets that commit back, so re-rendering adds no history. The ref is refs/renders/<id>, one per copy of the study and outside refs/heads/; it is not tagged or pushed, and main, its tags, HEAD and the checkpoint working tree are never touched. The call takes the checkpoint lock, so it stops while a checkpoint or another render holds it.

The commit only proves what the job was when the render began. A render that publishes outputs must also show that the code it executed matches the commit, and record what it published with study_render_record.

See also

study_render_record, study_checkpoint

Examples

# \donttest{
if (nzchar(Sys.which("git"))) {
  root <- file.path(tempdir(), "render-commit-example")
  study_setup(root, "Render commit example", 1L, renv = FALSE)
  writeLines("fit <- 1", file.path(root, "30_analyses", "fit.R"))
  # A commit needs an author; a real study uses the analyst's git config.
  withr::with_envvar(c(
    GIT_AUTHOR_NAME = "Example", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL = "example@example.org",
    GIT_COMMITTER_NAME = "Example", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL = "example@example.org"
  ), {
    sha <- study_render_commit("30_analyses/fit.R", root = root)
    print(substr(sha, 1, 7))
  })
  unlink(root, recursive = TRUE)
}
#> [1] "2082f56"
# }
